Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of Cisplatin vs DMSO, provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cells.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines were treated with cisplatin at IC₅₀ versus DMSO control and subjected to RNA-seq (three replicates per arm).  Differential expression followed by preranked GSEA (KEGG, GO BP, Reactome, MSigDB Hallmark) identified 23 KEGG, 77 GO BP, 22 Reactome and 7 Hallmark pathways enriched (FDR < 0.05).  Raw counts and metadata were provided; fold-changes and exact p-values not specified in user input.  

Keywords  
• p53 signaling  
• extracellular matrix (ECM)  
• apoptosis  
• ABC transporters  
• cell cycle  

Candidate Genes  
CDKN1A, BAX, MDM2, SERPINE1, IGFBP3, FAS

Analysis  
Cisplatin induces a dominant p53-mediated DNA damage response and apoptosis across all libraries (KEGG_2016 91% up, MSigDB Hallmark 100% up in p53 pathway).  ECM organization and ECM–receptor interactions rank among the top up-regulated KEGG and Reactome terms, coincident with GO BP signatures of inhibited cell migration/motility.  ABC transporters and allograft rejection pathways up-regulation suggest drug efflux and immune-related stress.  Metabolic and ion-transport processes appear in down-regulated GO BP (e.g., fructose metabolism, mitophagy) and Reactome (mitochondrial tRNA processing), indicating secondary metabolic adaptation.  Hallmark hypoxia, glycolysis and unfolded protein response are enriched, pointing to cellular stress.  

Targeted (p53-focused) Subset  
| Data Base                   | Pathway                                                       | Leading Genes                                |

| GO_Biological_Process_2023   | DNA damage response, signal transduction by p53 class mediator | CDKN1A, RPS27L, MDM2, PLK3, PIDD1, PLK2, TRIAP1 |
| GO_Biological_Process_2023   | Regulation of DNA damage response by p53 mediator             | CD74, PMAIP1, EEF1E1, SNAI2, MDM2, …           |
| Reactome_Pathways_2024       | TP53 regulates transcription of cell death genes              | TP53I3, TRIAP1, BCL2L14, PIDD1, TNFRSF10C, … |
| Reactome_Pathways_2024       | TP53 regulates transcription of cell cycle genes              | CDKN1A, BTG2, SFN, GADD45A, PLK3, CCNE2, …    |
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020         | p53 pathway                                                   | CDKN1A, XPC, NOTCH1, STOM, TRAF4, SFN, …      |

Discussion of p53 Subset  
All p53-related terms are up-regulated, reflecting cisplatin-induced DNA damage.  Core effectors CDKN1A (cell-cycle arrest), BAX (apoptosis), MDM2 (p53 feedback), IGFBP3 (growth inhibition) and SERPINE1 (ECM remodeling) appear as leading-edge genes, confirming a coordinated cell-cycle arrest/apoptotic program.

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Up-regulated  
| Gene      | Direction | Role/Function                                        | Pathway(s)                  |
|-----------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| CDKN1A    | UP        | Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor; G1 arrest         | p53 signaling, Hallmark p53 |
| BAX       | UP        | Pro-apoptotic BCL2 family member                     | p53 cell death, apoptosis   |
| MDM2      | UP        | E3 ligase for p53; negative feedback loop            | p53 signaling               |
| SERPINE1  | UP        | Plasminogen activator inhibitor; ECM remodeling      | ECM interaction, Hallmark   |
| IGFBP3    | UP        | IGF-binding protein; growth inhibition, apoptosis    | p53 pathway                 |

| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s)     |
|------|-----------|---------------|----------------|
| –    | –         | –             | –              |

Comparisons  
No tissue-specific contrasts were available; all signals derive from CRC cell lines.  The repeated detection of p53 activation across KEGG, Reactome and Hallmark underscores high-confidence DNA damage responses; solitary metabolic/mitophagy hits (e.g., PRKN) are lower-confidence, single-modality signals.

Implications  
Cisplatin triggers p53-mediated growth arrest and apoptosis in CRC, supports ECM reorganization that may impede metastasis, and induces ABC transporter expression that could underlie drug resistance.  Hallmark stress responses (hypoxia, UPR) suggest cisplatin-induced cellular stress beyond DNA damage.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate p53 pathway activation at protein level (p21, Bax) by Western blot.  
2. Test ABC transporter inhibitors to enhance cisplatin sensitivity.  
3. Perform migration/invasion assays to assess ECM remodeling impact.  
4. Measure autophagy/mitochondrial function given down-regulated mitophagy signatures.  

Explicit Targeted Check  
• Replication/cell-cycle: CDKN1A, CCNE2 up-regulated → observed.  
• Stress responses (UPR, hypoxia): enriched in Hallmark → observed.  
• Metabolism/mitochondria: glycolysis and mitophagy terms in Hallmark/GO → observed.
